fix_title: Verify the auxiliary output's parameter assignment with a diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a dealer-level diagnostic tool and read the auxiliary output configuration • 2. Confirm it matches the solenoid actually wired on the truck • 3. Correct the parameter and clear codes

fix_title: Replace the assigned solenoid valve
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air line and electrical connector • 2. Remove and replace the diff lock, transfer case, trailer or 3/2 valve solenoid • 3. Leak-check, clear codes and function-test

fix_title: Identify the assigned solenoid and inspect its connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Use the diagnostic tool to read which function (diff lock, transfer case, trailer, 3/2 valve) the output is configured for • 2. Locate and inspect that solenoid's connector for corrosion • 3. Clean, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the auxiliary output driver circuit for a short or open
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the output pin at the ECU and measure resistance to the solenoid coil • 2. Check for a short to ground or voltage along the harness • 3. Repair the wiring and re-test

fix_title: Re-seat and gauge the sensor air gap
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Loosen the sensor and push it fully against the tone ring • 2. Back it off per spec and lock it, checking with a 0.4 mm (0.016 in) feeler gauge • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Inspect and adjust wheel-bearing end play
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Jack the wheel and check for play with a dial indicator • 2. Re-torque or re-adjust the bearing per the axle spec, replacing bearings if worn • 3. Re-check the sensor air gap after adjustment

fix_title: Replace a chipped or bent tone (exciter) ring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the hub/axle assembly needed to access the tone ring • 2. Press off the damaged ring and press on the replacement • 3. Reassemble, set the sensor air gap and road-test

fix_title: Replace the wheel-speed sensor and mounting clip/bushing
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the worn sensor and its mounting bushing or clip • 2. Install the new sensor and bushing, seating it fully • 3. Set the air gap, clear codes and road-test

step_by_step_instructions: 1. Loosen the sensor and push it fully against the tone ring • 2. Back it off per spec and lock it, checking with a 0.4 mm (0.016 in) feeler gauge • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Replace a chipped or bent tone (exciter) ring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the hub/axle assembly needed to access the tone ring • 2. Press off the damaged ring and press on the replacement • 3. Reassemble, set the sensor air gap and road-test

fix_title: Replace the wheel-speed sensor and mounting clip/bushing
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the worn sensor and its mounting bushing or clip • 2. Install the new sensor and bushing, seating it fully • 3. Set the air gap, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Clean the tone ring and check sensor mounting security
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove debris and metal fines from the tone ring teeth • 2. Confirm the sensor is fully seated and not vibrating loose • 3. Clear codes and road-test through a speed range

fix_title: Replace a mismatched tire so the axle set matches
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Identify the tire(s) that do not match the axle set • 2. Replace with a correctly sized/matched tire • 3. Re-verify sizes and pressures, then clear codes

fix_title: Replace a worn or damaged tone ring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Access and remove the damaged tone ring • 2. Press on the replacement ring • 3. Reassemble, set the air gap and road-test

fix_title: Verify matched tire sizes and pressures across the axle
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure rolling circumference or check size/load ratings on each tire of the axle • 2. Correct pressure to spec on all positions • 3. Note any mismatched tire for replacement

fix_title: Verify wheel-speed sensor wiring matches the correct wheel position
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm each sensor connector is routed to its labeled ECU pin • 2. Correct any swapped or reversed left/right connections • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Inspect and clean the HSA valve/lamp connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the HSA valve or lamp connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Clean, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the HSA solenoid and lamp driver circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the HSA solenoid and lamp driver pins at the ECU • 2. Check for a short to ground or voltage, and for continuity to the component • 3. Repair the wiring and re-test

fix_title: Replace the HSA holding valve solenoid
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air line and electrical connector • 2. Remove and replace the HSA valve, torquing fittings per spec • 3. Leak-check, clear codes and function-test on a grade

fix_title: Inspect and clean the accelerator pedal position sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or oil/coolant intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test the accelerator pedal position sensor signal and supply circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe signal, ground and supply-voltage pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts and correct reference voltage • 3. Repair chafed wiring or corroded splices, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the accelerator pedal position sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify sensor air-gap or mounting per OEM spec • 2. Remove and replace the sensor and O-ring/seal • 3. Set the correct gap or torque, clear codes and verify signal quality on a scan tool

fix_title: Check the sensed target (gear teeth, reluctor ring, linkage) for damage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Inspect the reluctor wheel, gear teeth or mechanical linkage the sensor reads for damage, debris or wear • 2. Repair or replace the damaged component • 3. Reinstall the sensor, clear codes and verify

fix_title: Inspect and clean the fuel rail (common rail) pressure sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or moisture intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat the connector, clear codes and recheck live data

fix_title: Test the fuel rail (common rail) pressure sensor signal, ground and reference circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal, ground and 5V/8V reference pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts to ground/battery and resistance in range • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring, reseal splices, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the fuel rail (common rail) pressure sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the sensor's live reading against a known-good reference (scan tool or hand-held meter) • 2. Remove and replace the sensor, torque per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify the new reading tracks correctly

fix_title: Verify the underlying system condition the sensor is reporting
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm whether the out-of-range reading reflects a real system fault or a bad sensor • 2. Inspect the related system for the root physical cause • 3. Repair as needed, then clear codes and re-verify

fix_title: Inspect and clean the fuel injector connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the injector connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, heat damage or a loose crimp • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test the fuel injector driver circuit resistance and wiring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure coil/solenoid resistance at the connector against OEM spec • 2. Check the harness back to the ECU/injector driver for opens or shorts • 3. Repair or replace the harness section as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the fuel injector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm which cylinder/position is faulted from live data or cylinder cutout test • 2. Remove and replace the injector, use new seals/washers per OEM spec • 3. Torque to spec, prime the fuel system, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Perform injector trim/coding reset after service
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Enter the injector serial/trim code from the new injector into the ECU (or reset adaptive trims) using the OEM diagnostic tool • 2. Clear codes • 3. Verify smooth idle and no misfire/imbalance codes return

fix_title: Free and clean the cylinder misfire/power-balance monitor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the valve and inspect for sticking, varnish or debris • 2. Clean and free the moving element, or replace if seized • 3. Reinstall, clear codes and verify

fix_title: Check the related system pressure and condition
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify the system pressure the valve regulates is within spec with a gauge • 2. Address any upstream cause (restriction, pump wear, contamination) • 3. Clear codes and re-verify

fix_title: Replace the cylinder misfire/power-balance monitor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the valve/assembly • 2. Fit the replacement with new seals per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify correct operation

fix_title: Replace the engine pressure/temperature sensor (DCU-relayed)
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault follows the engine pressure/temperature sensor (DCU-relayed) and not the harness with a swap or resistance check • 2. Remove and replace the component, transferring any mounting hardware • 3. Clear codes and verify normal operation through a duty cycle

fix_title: Check engine pressure/temperature sensor (DCU-relayed) calibration/learned values with a service tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a service tool and compare the sensor's live reading against a known reference (refractometer for DEF quality, a second sensor, or a bench check) • 2. Run the OEM's sensor learn/reset procedure if the reading is offset but the circuit tests good • 3. Clear codes and confirm the reading holds through a duty cycle

fix_title: Inspect, clean and reseat the engine pressure/temperature sensor (DCU-relayed) connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the engine pressure/temperature sensor (DCU-relayed) circuit connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals and moisture intrusion, and check the harness for chafing near hot exhaust components • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes and confirm the fault does not return

fix_title: Test the engine pressure/temperature sensor (DCU-relayed) circuit for opens, shorts and correct supply voltage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the circuit at the connector with the harness connected • 2. Check for supply voltage, continuity to the controller and resistance to ground/battery • 3. Repair the open, shorted or chafed conductor, reseal the splice, clear codes

fix_title: Replace a failed NOx or urea-quality sensor that has gone silent
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm via the scan tool that the sensor itself, not just its wiring, has stopped responding • 2. Remove and replace the sensor per OEM torque and sealant specification • 3. Clear codes, run an aftertreatment regeneration/verification cycle and confirm the message returns

fix_title: Inspect the sending sensor/ECU connector and the shared backbone connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, identify the sensor (NOx, urea quality) or ECU that should be sending the missing message • 2. Inspect its connector and the nearest backbone/drop-line connector for corrosion or looseness, including DEF-line proximity corrosion • 3. Clean, reseat, clear codes and retest

fix_title: Verify power and ground at the sending sensor/ECU
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the sending device's power and ground pins • 2. Confirm battery/reference voltage is present and ground resistance is low • 3. Repair any open or corroded power or ground circuit found

fix_title: Confirm the sending device is present and addressing correctly on the bus
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a J1939 scan tool and watch for the expected message (e.g. TSC1, NOx sensor data) • 2. Confirm the device claims its expected source address and message rate • 3. If it never appears on the bus, treat it as failed and proceed to component-level diagnosis

fix_title: Inspect and clean the EGR valve actuator connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the EGR valve actuator • 2. Check pins for corrosion and the harness for chafing or heat damage near the exhaust • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes and cycle the actuator with a service tool

fix_title: Test the EGR valve actuator motor/coil circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the motor or coil circuit at the connector • 2. Check winding resistance against spec and continuity/insulation to ground • 3. Repair chafed or shorted wiring, clear codes and re-test with a commanded sweep

fix_title: Replace the EGR valve actuator
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the EGR valve actuator assembly and its gasket/clamp • 2. Install the replacement, torque fasteners per spec and reconnect the harness • 3. Clear codes, run the actuator's self-calibration/learn procedure if the OEM tool supports one, and confirm normal operation

fix_title: Free up and clean a sticking EGR valve actuator
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the EGR valve actuator (or access it in place per OEM procedure) • 2. Clean carbon and soot buildup from the bore/shaft with an approved solvent, working the shaft through its full travel • 3. Reinstall, clear codes and command a full-range sweep with a service tool to confirm smooth travel

fix_title: Replace the throttle position sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify sensor air-gap or mounting per OEM spec • 2. Remove and replace the sensor and O-ring/seal • 3. Set the correct gap or torque, clear codes and verify signal quality on a scan tool

fix_title: Inspect and clean the throttle position sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or oil/coolant intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test the throttle position sensor signal and supply circuits

fix_title: Test the engine oil pressure sensor signal, ground and reference circuits

fix_title: Inspect and clean the ambient/barometric pressure sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or moisture intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat the connector, clear codes and recheck live data

fix_title: Test the ambient/barometric pressure sensor signal, ground and reference circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal, ground and 5V/8V reference pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts to ground/battery and resistance in range • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring, reseal splices, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the ambient/barometric pressure sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the sensor's live reading against a known-good reference (scan tool or hand-held meter) • 2. Remove and replace the sensor, torque per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify the new reading tracks correctly

fix_title: Verify the underlying system condition the sensor is reporting
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm whether the out-of-range reading reflects a real system fault or a bad sensor • 2. Inspect the related system for the root physical cause • 3. Repair as needed, then clear codes and re-verify

fix_title: Check and top up the fluid level
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check the level with the engine off on level ground against the dipstick/sight glass • 2. Top up with the correct fluid to the full mark • 3. Clear codes and recheck after a run cycle

fix_title: Replace the level sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the actual fluid level is correct (rules out a genuine low-level condition) • 2. Remove and replace the level sensor/float • 3. Clear codes and verify the reading tracks correctly

fix_title: Test the level-sensor signal circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the sensor signal and ground pins • 2. Check for an open or short in the harness • 3. Repair as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the switch
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the switch from the panel or chassis mount • 2. Install a new switch of the same type and rating • 3. Reconnect, cycle the switch and confirm the ESC reads the correct state

fix_title: Inspect and clean the switch connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the switch connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, spread terminals • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and cycle the switch to confirm operation

fix_title: Test the switch input circuit to the body controller
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the input pin at the body controller while cycling the switch • 2. Check for the expected reference voltage and continuity to the switch • 3. Repair any open, short or corroded splice, clear and re-check

fix_title: Verify the switch input configuration in Diamond Logic Builder
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect Diamond Logic Builder and read the switch input configuration • 2. Confirm the input logic (normally open/closed) matches the installed switch • 3. Reteach or reprogram if mismatched, then clear codes

fix_title: Replace the engine control unit (ECU) (or the affected internal module)
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault persists after a reflash and clean power/ground • 2. Replace the ECU/module and transfer or re-program its configuration data • 3. Clear codes and verify with a full system scan

fix_title: Reflash/reprogram the engine control unit (ECU) with the latest calibration
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the OEM diagnostic tool and check for a newer software/calibration release • 2. Reflash the ECU per the OEM procedure • 3. Clear codes, run a full DTC scan and road-test

fix_title: Check ECU power, ground and case-connector integrity
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, inspect the main ECU harness connectors for corrosion, bent pins or moisture intrusion • 2. Check the ECU's power and ground straps for a clean, tight connection • 3. Reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test ECU supply and ground circuit wiring for the affected channel
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify battery voltage reaches the ECU's power pins with the key on • 2. Check chassis ground points for corrosion or a poor connection • 3. Repair as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Inspect and clean the fuel injector connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the injector connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, heat damage or a loose crimp • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the fuel injector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm which cylinder/position is faulted from live data or cylinder cutout test • 2. Remove and replace the injector, use new seals/washers per OEM spec • 3. Torque to spec, prime the fuel system, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Test the fuel injector driver circuit resistance and wiring

fix_title: Perform injector trim/coding reset after service
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Enter the injector serial/trim code from the new injector into the ECU (or reset adaptive trims) using the OEM diagnostic tool • 2. Clear codes • 3. Verify smooth idle and no misfire/imbalance codes return

fix_title: Test the turbocharger wastegate/bypass actuator driver circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure coil resistance against OEM spec • 2. Check the drive and return wiring for opens or shorts to ground/battery • 3. Repair as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Inspect and clean the turbocharger wastegate/bypass actuator connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the actuator connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion or a loose crimp • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the turbocharger wastegate/bypass actuator
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the actuator/solenoid and inspect the mating bore or linkage for wear or contamination • 2. Fit the replacement with new seals per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify commanded movement on a scan tool

fix_title: Free and verify mechanical movement of the actuated component
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check the actuator moves the linkage/valve through its full range without binding or sticking • 2. Clean or free a sticking mechanism, or replace if seized • 3. Clear codes and re-verify commanded response

fix_title: Inspect and clean the fuel rail (common rail) pressure sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or moisture intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat the connector, clear codes and recheck live data

fix_title: Reprogram or update the linked device's configuration/firmware
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the OEM service tool to the ECU that owns the proprietary link • 2. Check for a required configuration file or firmware update for the linked device • 3. Apply the update, clear codes and confirm normal communication resumes

fix_title: Replace the linked smart sensor, actuator or gateway/bridge module
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm via the OEM tool that the linked device itself, not just its wiring, has stopped communicating • 2. Remove and replace the smart sensor, actuator or gateway/bridge module • 3. Clear codes and confirm the link re-establishes on the next power cycle

fix_title: Inspect the sub-network or smart-device connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, identify the smart sensor/actuator or the proprietary 'Machine'/implement CAN segment reporting the fault • 2. Inspect its connector and any bridge/gateway connector on that segment for corrosion or looseness • 3. Clean, reseat, clear codes and retest

fix_title: Verify power, ground and continuity on the proprietary link
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the linked device's power and ground pins and confirm battery voltage and a clean ground • 2. Check continuity and check for a short to power or ground on the dedicated sub-network pair • 3. Repair any wiring fault found

fix_title: Replace the NOx sensor, upstream of SCR
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault follows the NOx sensor, upstream of SCR and not the harness with a swap or resistance check • 2. Remove and replace the sensor at its mounting boss (exhaust pipe for NOx/O2/NH3 sensors, DEF tank for a quality sensor), torquing/sealing per spec - these are heated, CAN-networked smart sensors; aftermarket HD units commonly run $300-700 • 3. Clear codes, allow the sensor to complete its power-up self-test, and verify normal operation through a duty cycle

fix_title: Check NOx sensor, upstream of SCR calibration/learned values with a service tool

fix_title: Replace the regulator/relay supplying the 5V/8V sensor supply rail
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the supply is out of spec at the ECU's own output pin (points to the ECU/regulator, not the wiring) • 2. Replace the affected relay or, if internal, the ECU • 3. Clear codes and verify

fix_title: Inspect connectors on all circuits fed by the 5V/8V sensor supply rail
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, inspect every sensor connector sharing this supply rail for corrosion or water intrusion • 2. Clean and reseat as needed • 3. Clear codes and recheck rail voltage

fix_title: Test the 5V/8V sensor supply rail for a short or excessive load
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure the supply rail voltage at the ECU connector against OEM spec with all sensors connected, then with each disconnected in turn • 2. Isolate the shorted or overloaded branch • 3. Repair the wiring/sensor causing the short, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the DEF tank heating valve
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault follows the DEF tank heating valve and not the harness with a swap or resistance check • 2. Remove and replace the component, transferring any mounting hardware • 3. Clear codes and verify normal operation through a duty cycle

fix_title: Inspect, clean and reseat the DEF tank heating valve connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the DEF tank heating valve circuit connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals and moisture intrusion, and check the harness for chafing near hot exhaust components • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes and confirm the fault does not return

fix_title: Test the DEF tank heating valve circuit for opens, shorts and correct supply voltage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the circuit at the connector with the harness connected • 2. Check for supply voltage, continuity to the controller and resistance to ground/battery • 3. Repair the open, shorted or chafed conductor, reseal the splice, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the DEF line heater
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault follows the DEF line heater and not the harness with a swap or resistance check • 2. Remove and replace the component, transferring any mounting hardware • 3. Clear codes and verify normal operation through a duty cycle

fix_title: Inspect, clean and reseat the DEF line heater connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the DEF line heater circuit connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals and moisture intrusion, and check the harness for chafing near hot exhaust components • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes and confirm the fault does not return

fix_title: Test the DEF line heater circuit for opens, shorts and correct supply voltage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the circuit at the connector with the harness connected • 2. Check for supply voltage, continuity to the controller and resistance to ground/battery • 3. Repair the open, shorted or chafed conductor, reseal the splice, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the SCR catalyst temperature sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm engine is cool enough to work near the exhaust • 2. Remove the SCR catalyst temperature sensor from its boss in the exhaust stream, note anti-seize on the new sensor's threads • 3. fix_title: Inspect and clean the intake or charge-air temperature sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or moisture intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat the connector, clear codes and recheck live data

fix_title: Test the intake or charge-air temperature sensor signal, ground and reference circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal, ground and 5V/8V reference pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts to ground/battery and resistance in range • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring, reseal splices, clear codes

fix_title: Inspect and clean the ignition coil connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the actuator connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion or a loose crimp • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test the ignition coil driver circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure coil resistance against OEM spec • 2. Check the drive and return wiring for opens or shorts to ground/battery • 3. Repair as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the ignition coil
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the actuator/solenoid and inspect the mating bore or linkage for wear or contamination • 2. Fit the replacement with new seals per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify commanded movement on a scan tool

fix_title: Free and verify mechanical movement of the actuated component
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check the actuator moves the linkage/valve through its full range without binding or sticking • 2. Clean or free a sticking mechanism, or replace if seized • 3. Clear codes and re-verify commanded response

fix_title: Inspect, clean and reseat the aftertreatment lambda (O2) sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the aftertreatment lambda (O2) sensor circuit connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals and moisture intrusion, and check the harness for chafing near hot exhaust components • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes and confirm the fault does not return

fix_title: Test the aftertreatment lambda (O2) sensor heater, signal and CAN sub-network circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the heater supply, signal and network pins at the connector • 2. Check for battery voltage at the heater pin, correct signal reference and continuity/termination on the sensor's local CAN sub-network • 3. Repair the open, shorted or chafed conductor, reseal the splice, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the aftertreatment lambda (O2) sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault follows the aftertreatment lambda (O2) sensor and not the harness with a swap or resistance check • 2. Remove and replace the sensor at its mounting boss (exhaust pipe for NOx/O2/NH3 sensors, DEF tank for a quality sensor), torquing/sealing per spec - these are heated, CAN-networked smart sensors; aftermarket HD units commonly run $300-700 • 3. Clear codes, allow the sensor to complete its power-up self-test, and verify normal operation through a duty cycle

fix_title: Check aftertreatment lambda (O2) sensor calibration/learned values with a service tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a service tool and compare the sensor's live reading against a known reference (refractometer for DEF quality, a second sensor, or a bench check) • 2. Run the OEM's sensor learn/reset procedure if the reading is offset but the circuit tests good • 3. Clear codes and confirm the reading holds through a duty cycle

fix_title: Replace the bank fuel-trim monitor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the sensor's live reading against a known-good reference (scan tool or hand-held meter) • 2. Remove and replace the sensor, torque per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify the new reading tracks correctly

fix_title: Inspect and clean the bank fuel-trim monitor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or moisture intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat the connector, clear codes and recheck live data

fix_title: Test the bank fuel-trim monitor signal, ground and reference circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal, ground and 5V/8V reference pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts to ground/battery and resistance in range • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring, reseal splices, clear codes

fix_title: Inspect and clean the ambient/barometric pressure sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or moisture intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat the connector, clear codes and recheck live data

fix_title: Test the ambient/barometric pressure sensor signal, ground and reference circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal, ground and 5V/8V reference pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts to ground/battery and resistance in range • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring, reseal splices, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the ambient/barometric pressure sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the sensor's live reading against a known-good reference (scan tool or hand-held meter) • 2. Remove and replace the sensor, torque per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify the new reading tracks correctly

fix_title: Verify the underlying system condition the sensor is reporting
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm whether the out-of-range reading reflects a real system fault or a bad sensor • 2. Inspect the related system for the root physical cause • 3. Repair as needed, then clear codes and re-verify

fix_title: Remove and thermally clean or replace the EGR cooler
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the EGR cooler from the exhaust and inspect the substrate for cracking or excessive ash cake • 2. Send for professional thermal/pneumatic cleaning (or replace if cracked or beyond cleaning spec) with a before/after weight or backpressure reading • 3. Reinstall with new gaskets/clamps, reset the ash/soot service counter with a service tool and clear codes

fix_title: Replace the differential pressure sensor and lines feeding the EGR cooler estimate
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the estimate tracks a known-bad or known-good differential pressure sensor reading before condemning the filter • 2. Replace the sensor and/or clear the pressure lines if plugged or swapped • 3. Clear codes and re-run the estimate through a duty cycle

fix_title: Run a parked (stationary) forced regeneration with a service tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a J1939 service tool and confirm no active inhibits (low fuel, low DEF, open door/parking brake requirements per OEM) • 2. Command a parked regeneration and monitor DPF inlet temperature climbs into the regeneration window • 3. Let the cycle complete, then re-read the EGR cooler estimate and clear codes if it has dropped to normal

fix_title: Reset the EGR cooler service counter after filter service
step_by_step_instructions: 1. After a cleaned or replaced filter is reinstalled, connect a service tool • 2. Reset the ash/soot load counter to zero per the OEM procedure • 3. Clear codes and confirm the estimate starts climbing from zero on the next duty cycle

fix_title: Replace the sensor or actuator on this circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Identify the physical component tied to this manufacturer-specific parameter from the OEM wiring diagram or dealer tool • 2. Replace the component • 3. Clear codes and verify

fix_title: Inspect and clean the connector for this parameter's circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the connector serving this circuit (identify via the pin-out for this SPN in the OEM wiring diagram) • 2. Check pins for corrosion or a loose crimp • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test the circuit for an open, short or out-of-range voltage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the affected pin(s) at the module connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts to ground/battery and correct reference voltage against the OEM wiring diagram • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring, clear codes

fix_title: Identify the assigned solenoid and inspect its connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Use the diagnostic tool to read which function (diff lock, transfer case, trailer, 3/2 valve) the output is configured for • 2. Locate and inspect that solenoid's connector for corrosion • 3. Clean, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the auxiliary output driver circuit for a short or open
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the output pin at the ECU and measure resistance to the solenoid coil • 2. Check for a short to ground or voltage along the harness • 3. Repair the wiring and re-test

fix_title: Replace the assigned solenoid valve
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air line and electrical connector • 2. Remove and replace the diff lock, transfer case, trailer or 3/2 valve solenoid • 3. Leak-check, clear codes and function-test

fix_title: Verify the auxiliary output's parameter assignment with a diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a dealer-level diagnostic tool and read the auxiliary output configuration • 2. Confirm it matches the solenoid actually wired on the truck • 3. Correct the parameter and clear codes

fix_title: Replace the wheel-speed sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the old sensor and clean the bore • 2. Fit the new sensor and set the air gap per spec • 3. Reconnect, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Replace the sensor pigtail/extension harness
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Disconnect the failed pigtail at the sensor and at the chassis harness • 2. Route and secure the new pigtail away from moving parts • 3. Reconnect, clear codes and verify a clean speed trace

fix_title: Clear codes and confirm the fault does not return
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Clear stored and active codes with a diagnostic tool • 2. Road-test through a speed range • 3. Re-scan to confirm the SPN/FMI has not reset

fix_title: Inspect and clean the wheel-speed sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, moisture and spread terminals • 3. Clean, apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Trace and repair the sensor wiring harness
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the sensor pins at the ECU and measure coil resistance • 2. Follow the harness to the axle looking for chafe points and pinches • 3. Repair or splice the damaged run, reseal and re-test

fix_title: Verify matched tire sizes and pressures across the axle
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure rolling circumference or check size/load ratings on each tire of the axle • 2. Correct pressure to spec on all positions • 3. Note any mismatched tire for replacement

fix_title: Replace a worn or damaged tone ring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Access and remove the damaged tone ring • 2. Press on the replacement ring • 3. Reassemble, set the air gap and road-test

fix_title: Verify wheel-speed sensor wiring matches the correct wheel position
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm each sensor connector is routed to its labeled ECU pin • 2. Correct any swapped or reversed left/right connections • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Clean the tone ring and check sensor mounting security
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove debris and metal fines from the tone ring teeth • 2. Confirm the sensor is fully seated and not vibrating loose • 3. Clear codes and road-test through a speed range

fix_title: Replace a mismatched tire so the axle set matches
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Identify the tire(s) that do not match the axle set • 2. Replace with a correctly sized/matched tire • 3. Re-verify sizes and pressures, then clear codes

fix_title: Run the treadle sensor calibration/learn procedure with a diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the dealer diagnostic tool • 2. Follow the prompted pedal-travel calibration sequence • 3. Verify both channels track together and clear codes

fix_title: Replace the brake demand (treadle valve) sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the treadle valve/pedal sensor assembly • 2. Install the replacement sensor and reconnect the harness • 3. Clear codes and run the calibration procedure

fix_title: Inspect and clean the treadle valve sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the treadle valve sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Clean, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the primary and secondary sensor circuits for continuity
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the primary and secondary signal pins at the ECU • 2. Check continuity and reference voltage on each channel • 3. Repair the harness and re-test

fix_title: Confirm the ECU part number matches the vehicle's axle and sensor count
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Record the ECU part number and the vehicle's actual axle/sensor/modulator layout • 2. Cross-check against the OEM part-number table or contact the vehicle OEM • 3. Order the correct ECU if mismatched

fix_title: Replace an ECU programmed for the wrong configuration
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Order the ECU matching the vehicle's confirmed configuration • 2. Install and complete dealer end-of-line programming • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Re-run the ESC/ABS end-of-line configuration in the diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a dealer-level diagnostic tool • 2. Enter the correct sensor count, modulator count and ESC enable/disable settings for the vehicle • 3. Save, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Re-learn the steering-angle-sensor center/ratio
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Center the steering wheel with the vehicle on level ground, wheels straight • 2. Run the steering-angle learn procedure in the diagnostic tool • 3. Verify the learned value and clear codes

fix_title: Verify wheel-speed sensor wiring matches the correct wheel position
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm each sensor connector is routed to its labeled ECU pin • 2. Correct any swapped or reversed left/right connections • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Replace a worn or damaged tone ring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Access and remove the damaged tone ring • 2. Press on the replacement ring • 3. Reassemble, set the air gap and road-test

fix_title: Clean the tone ring and check sensor mounting security
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove debris and metal fines from the tone ring teeth • 2. Confirm the sensor is fully seated and not vibrating loose • 3. Clear codes and road-test through a speed range

fix_title: Replace a mismatched tire so the axle set matches
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Identify the tire(s) that do not match the axle set • 2. Replace with a correctly sized/matched tire • 3. Re-verify sizes and pressures, then clear codes

fix_title: Verify matched tire sizes and pressures across the axle
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure rolling circumference or check size/load ratings on each tire of the axle • 2. Correct pressure to spec on all positions • 3. Note any mismatched tire for replacement

fix_title: Inspect the valve for sticking or an internal air leak causing extra cycling
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Listen for continuous air flow or chatter at the valve during a static ABS self-test • 2. Cycle the valve with a diagnostic tool and observe response • 3. Note the valve for replacement if it sticks or leaks

fix_title: Recheck the related wheel-speed signal that may be triggering excess ABS activity
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Review stored wheel-speed fault history for the same wheel position • 2. Inspect that sensor's air gap and tone ring condition • 3. Correct the wheel-speed fault before re-testing the valve

fix_title: Replace the overheated ABS modulator valve
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air lines and electrical connector • 2. Remove and replace the modulator valve, torquing fittings per spec • 3. Leak-check, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Check the affected valve's coil resistance for a partial short
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the modulator valve's coil pins and measure resistance against spec • 2. Compare against the other wheel positions for a low reading • 3. Repair the wiring or flag the valve for replacement

fix_title: Replace the ECU if the checksum fault returns after reprogramming
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the checksum fault repeats after a full parameter reload • 2. Replace the ECU with the correct part number • 3. Complete dealer end-of-line programming and configuration

fix_title: Re-load the vehicle configuration parameters with a dealer diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the dealer diagnostic tool • 2. Re-enter or re-load the affected parameter group (traction control, brake, gravity/vehicle, axle configuration) • 3. Save, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Cycle ignition and re-scan; a transient checksum error may clear
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Record the active fault • 2. Cycle the ignition off and on • 3. Re-scan to see if the checksum fault clears

fix_title: Update the aftertreatment DCU's firmware/calibration if a service bulletin applies
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check for an applicable OEM software update or service bulletin for this fault • 2. Reflash with the latest calibration using the OEM service tool • 3. Clear codes and confirm the fault does not return through a duty cycle

fix_title: Inspect the aftertreatment DCU's wiring, grounds and power connectors
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, inspect the connectors and ground straps feeding the aftertreatment DCU • 2. Check for corrosion, loose terminals or a poor ground • 3. Clean/repair, reseat, clear codes and re-test

fix_title: Replace the aftertreatment DCU
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault is internal to the aftertreatment DCU and not its wiring or power supply first • 2. Remove and replace the module per OEM procedure, including any required re-flash or configuration • 3. Clear codes and confirm normal operation through a duty cycle

fix_title: Inspect the aftertreatment DCU power supply's wiring, grounds and power connectors
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, inspect the connectors and ground straps feeding the aftertreatment DCU power supply • 2. Check for corrosion, loose terminals or a poor ground • 3. Clean/repair, reseat, clear codes and re-test

fix_title: Replace the aftertreatment DCU power supply
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault is internal to the aftertreatment DCU power supply and not its wiring or power supply first • 2. Remove and replace the module per OEM procedure, including any required re-flash or configuration • 3. Clear codes and confirm normal operation through a duty cycle

fix_title: Update the aftertreatment DCU power supply's firmware/calibration if a service bulletin applies
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check for an applicable OEM software update or service bulletin for this fault • 2. Reflash with the latest calibration using the OEM service tool • 3. Clear codes and confirm the fault does not return through a duty cycle

fix_title: Clear the DEF supply module pump's inlet strainer and suction line of blockage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Relieve system pressure and disconnect the suction line at the tank • 2. Pull the in-tank strainer and clear crystallized DEF or debris; check the suction line and fittings for a loose connection drawing air • 3. Reinstall, prime per OEM procedure, clear codes and confirm pressure builds normally

fix_title: Replace the DEF supply module pump
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Relieve system pressure and disconnect DEF lines and the electrical connector at the DEF supply module pump • 2. Remove and replace the module/pump assembly with new seals per OEM procedure • 3. Prime the system, clear codes and confirm pressure and flow reach spec

fix_title: Inspect and clean the DEF supply module pump connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the DEF supply module pump • 2. Check pins for corrosion and DEF crystal deposits (a white crusty residue) that block the terminals • 3. Clean, apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test the DEF supply module pump power, ground and control circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the power, ground and PWM/control signal pins at the connector • 2. Check for battery voltage at the power pin, a clean ground and a valid control signal from the DCU • 3. Repair the faulted circuit, clear codes and re-test

fix_title: Replace the fuel injector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm which cylinder/position is faulted from live data or cylinder cutout test • 2. Remove and replace the injector, use new seals/washers per OEM spec • 3. Torque to spec, prime the fuel system, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Inspect and clean the fuel injector connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the injector connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, heat damage or a loose crimp • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test the fuel injector driver circuit resistance and wiring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure coil/solenoid resistance at the connector against OEM spec • 2. Check the harness back to the ECU/injector driver for opens or shorts • 3. Repair or replace the harness section as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Perform injector trim/coding reset after service
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Enter the injector serial/trim code from the new injector into the ECU (or reset adaptive trims) using the OEM diagnostic tool • 2. Clear codes • 3. Verify smooth idle and no misfire/imbalance codes return

fix_title: Inspect the sub-network or smart-device connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, identify the smart sensor/actuator or the proprietary 'Machine'/implement CAN segment reporting the fault • 2. Inspect its connector and any bridge/gateway connector on that segment for corrosion or looseness • 3. Clean, reseat, clear codes and retest

fix_title: Reprogram or update the linked device's configuration/firmware
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the OEM service tool to the ECU that owns the proprietary link • 2. Check for a required configuration file or firmware update for the linked device • 3. Apply the update, clear codes and confirm normal communication resumes

fix_title: Replace the linked smart sensor, actuator or gateway/bridge module
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm via the OEM tool that the linked device itself, not just its wiring, has stopped communicating • 2. Remove and replace the smart sensor, actuator or gateway/bridge module • 3. Clear codes and confirm the link re-establishes on the next power cycle

fix_title: Verify power, ground and continuity on the proprietary link
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the linked device's power and ground pins and confirm battery voltage and a clean ground • 2. Check continuity and check for a short to power or ground on the dedicated sub-network pair • 3. Repair any wiring fault found
